rss_stopping_distance — DRIVE rss op

• Data kinds: none → scalar (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.rss_stopping_distance(v: 'float', rho: 'float', accel: 'float', brake: 'float', v_max: 'Optional[float]' = None, direction: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'float' (to call the implementation directly, import rsssafety; rsssafety.rss_stopping_distance(v: 'float', rho: 'float', accel: 'float', brake: 'float', v_max: 'Optional[float]' = None, direction: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'float'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("rss_stopping_distance"))

Usage

Signed position offset under ad-rss-lib's stated braking pattern (1 formula shared by the longitudinal and lateral directions).

Accelerates with accel during ρ (capped at v_max), and adds the stopping distance direction · v_ρ > 0 only when the speed v_ρ after ρ is heading toward the other vehicle (direction · v_ρ² / (2 brake)). If heading away, it is not added (the calculateLongitudinalDistanceOffsetAfterStatedBrakingPattern test in the lib's calculateLateralDistanceOffsetAfterStatedBrakingPattern / signbit).

Sign convention

• direction = direction toward the other vehicle (+1 or −1). Longitudinally +1 (direction of travel = +x). Laterally, the left vehicle is +1 and the right vehicle −1.

• v is a signed speed (positive on the direction side means heading toward the other vehicle). Longitudinally, call with v ≥ 0.

• accel is signed and pointed to the direction side (ValueError unless direction · accel ≥ 0). Longitudinally +a_accel_max; laterally, left +a_lat, right −a_lat.

• brake is a positive magnitude. It always acts "in the direction that brings the speed toward the other vehicle to 0" (= the −direction side).

• v_max is the upper limit of the reached speed on the direction side (None = no limit). If |v| is already at or above it, no acceleration occurs.

Longitudinally (v ≥ 0, accel ≥ 0) this becomes v ρ + ½ a ρ² + (v + a ρ)²/(2 b), matching the travel distance of the following vehicle in Lemma 2 of the paper.
